This window the migration finally has an order and a route. Order: simplest first - ZM Legal and Opterra are the targets, with the outliers deferred (First Ring for products, subscriptions, discounts and e-invoicing; JSN Crowd Events for decimal quantities and credit-note volume; Lionheart Music for online payments; Total Bathrooms for mixed products and free-form lines). Only three cohort-2 customers actively use WeFact invoicing at all. Route: rather than wait for neno invoicing to reach WeFact parity, integrate the WeFact API and process invoices raised in WeFact through neno's reconciliation path - roughly one week of Dmytro's time to make the simpler customers migration-ready. The mechanism for the 14 August transition-date guidance also landed: a per-workspace transition date now decides which transactions neno reconciles and exports (NEO-1897), alongside a scheduled pull of WeFact documents into the review queue (NEO-1922). What still gates migration is the invoicing feature list, and it is long: reminders unbuilt, no payment link on invoices, no past-due indicator, the cancelled state not triggering, decimal and negative quantities and prices unsupported, credit-note presentation wrong, no multi-currency for the one cohort customer invoicing in USD. Frederique was closing the MVP issues on 19 August with an MVP planning call set for the next morning, but engineers are stretched. Two operational items carried: Ocean Ionics' team is still forwarding bills by hand, so bills go missing, and it is unresolved whether new customers connect their banks via Lendroom or neno's own open banking.

fef38f90-b82c-4c47-b377-6dcb9b1a3020.exec_summary: Goal: file Q3 VAT for five neno customers out of neno's own double-entry ledger by 30 Sep. The ledger has been live on production for Ocean Ionics since 22 Jul; the work is now almost entirely about closing the defects the first 19-day run surfaced, where 49 of 138 ledger events never booked. That close-out moved this window: Mark landed a documented break-the-glass procedure for repairing written ledger events (NEO-1796, 18 Aug), fixed a GL allocation that booked even when the transaction's import leg had never been booked (NEO-1932, 19 Aug), and is now replacing ledgerState with an open-correction lock plus a derived recognition, because today every bill reports itself as booked (NEO-1971, in progress). His 18 Aug project update - titled "Recovering from failed Ledger Events caused by bookkeeping bugs" - reads On track. The strategic decision the quarter hangs on has not moved. Mark and Matthew were due to reconvene on Friday 14 August on the Ocean Ionics fork - backfill neno's ledger from Exact and take source-of-truth status from a clean cut-off, or keep filing VAT in Exact - and six days later there is still no call, while the Belastingdienst reconciliation strategy is needed before the start of September. Underneath it, the filing depends on a reconciliation backlog that got measured this week: 79 Ocean Ionics transactions in neno, only 23 with a corresponding bill pending review, 56 unmatched - and the bill search accountants use to find the counterpart bill truncates its results at volume (a 30 June Wildkamp bill of EUR 10.65 was on the list but absent from search). Q2 is also not clean: Andries closed it early in Exact with manual entries there, and the matching Q2 debit transfers and bills are still open in neno. Two design threads were deliberately parked - manual entries ("too many variants to resolve in stand-up", moved to a Matthew/Dmytro catch-up) and bulk direct-debit matching, where one Monday sweep settles several prior-week invoices but the reconciliation API only ever surfaces one best match.
whats_changed: 24 Aug, Granola (Backfill & Manual Entries): the ledger event model was locked - the queue books solely from payload facts at booking time (no source lookup or inference after the fact); editing a booked bill now requires two explicit steps (remove ledger entry and edit, then confirm and rebook) instead of the previous live-edit flow.
24 Aug: async Exact booking proposed (trigger off the reconciliation ledger event rather than synchronously) - not yet decided, needs wider team validation.

26 Aug, Granola (Multi-Currency in Exact): a new EUR/USD customer forced a multi-currency decision - all entries write to Exact in EUR for now with FX conversion for reporting, USD kept as a separate account while active; whether Exact's ledger can actually handle multi-currency is unconfirmed with Yako, and FX write-offs need Jean Lava's input once accounting is involved.

19 and 24 Aug, Granola: Ocean Ionics remains in a messy transition state with no hard cutover date - proposed fix is to backfill historical data using external proof, then set a clean cutover date; Q2 items Andrew reconciled in Exact are still unconfirmed against neno.

'Close out the ledger's first production run' remains a Linear project under this initiative with no board card (needs-triage, carried over from prior runs) - active this window on grouped-match settlement (NEO-2056) and missing booked bills (NEO-1991), both Mark.

risks.text: The Ocean Ionics fork - backfill neno's ledger from Exact and take source-of-truth status from a clean cut-off, or keep filing VAT in Exact - still has no decision six days after the 14 Aug reconvene was due, while the Belastingdienst reconciliation strategy is needed before the start of September.

The ledger queue does not drain: between 33% and 47% of import events stalled every week since go-live, a rate that is not decaying, and the failure surface under-reported by roughly a factor of five (9 of 49 on the 2026-08-10 reading). Q3 filing from neno depends on closing this.

decisions.text: Ledger event model locked: the queue books solely from payload facts at booking time, with no source lookup or inference after the fact. decisions.text: VAT code semantics and document reconciliation are separated: for reverse_charge, import_vat and intra_eu_acquisition the document-side rate is effectively 0% (net = base, VAT = 0, gross = base), while the code keeps its 21% for the ledger and the VAT return. Filed as NEO-1890, related to NEO-1208.

The interim "convert to 0% when sending to Exact" agreement was reversed the same day: purchase-entry-sync keeps posting the VAT code verbatim, because Exact applies its own treatment from its own code definition and a 0% would drop the reverse-charge legs on Exact's side. The scope of the fix is the VAT treatment/code, not the vendor's country.

Onboarding guidance adopted for customers whose books already live in Exact: a defined transition date per customer, Swan/Open Banking/WeFact/NMBRS cut off from Exact and enabled on neno on that date, Exact spillover cleaned out and neno backfilled to the transition date. Reconciliation is routed by transaction date - after it on neno, before it in Exact - and the two modes must never overlap on one transaction.

The net VAT position books to an ordinary payable/receivable with the Belastingdienst as counterparty, the tax authority modelled as an ordinary party - so a VAT return is literally a bill being paid and reuses the existing matching, settlement and outstanding-balance machinery.

"Supplementary return" is split into two distinct outcomes - supplementing the next regular return versus filing a separate correction return for that period - and the one-account-or-a-pair question for corrections was dropped.

Each VAT period is cleared by a counter-booking that zeroes the VAT ledger accounts and posts the net to a VAT suspense account classified as a general account, not a VAT account. The 5 Aug error came from allocating a transaction directly to the BTW receivable account (1520 range), which is blocked by design.

The VAT submission task gets its own dedicated email template that points the customer to the platform rather than carrying sensitive detail inline, and the VAT upload is modelled as a new task type depositing a document into the vault with transaction info left empty so it never surfaces in the reconciliation queue.

Andries/Art reconciliation & GL-coding session (fuller readout, previously uncaptured): manual GL/VAT selection remains the core pain point for Andries - recalling vendor context and the applicable VAT rate on every invoice, including cases needing two VAT-coded lines on one receipt (e.g. fuel vs non-fuel items). Smart Bill Review VAT coding made arithmetic rather than guessed (NEO-1595, Art, In Review 28 Jul): the coding proposer's prompt carried the supplier name, each line's position and description and the two candidate lists, but withheld net, gross, tax rate and the bill-level tax entries - so the model had to guess the VAT rate and whether amounts were inclusive or exclusive. The fix derives the rate and inclusive/exclusive treatment from the bill's own figures and narrows the candidates accordingly; PR #1266 closes the Albert Heijn receipt case Matthew raised the same day.

Smart Bill Review GL/VAT coding pipeline landed its core pieces: the proposal engine runs as a pipeline step that persists a validated GL+VAT proposal (or an abstention) per bill line, checked against the workspace's Exact code lists (NEO-1531/A2, Done 26 Jul); a broken proposer is now surfaced instead of silently abstaining (NEO-1567, Done 27 Jul); and a prod bug that left the bill detail page permanently read-only was fixed - BillDetailContent fetched Exact status with a bare relative URL, hit app.neno.co in production, got the SPA index.html and concluded Exact was disconnected, so the GL/VAT pickers never mounted (NEO-1578, Done 27 Jul).

Smart Bill Review GL/VAT coding assistance (Art): the bill-parsing model is being extended to present precise GL-account and VAT-code recommendations to accountants, learned from historical supplier bookings (Ocean Ionics VAT & GL code matching); ~70-80% accuracy on limited data. VAT is attributed in full to the period the invoice was issued, even when the underlying expense is recognised across multiple periods (subscriptions spread the expense, never the VAT); non-EU regimes (e.g. South Africa) out of scope for current VAT logic.

Settlement amount validation (Decision 08 / INV-30): reconciliation checks amount, not just zero-balance - the bank-entry leg and the bill leg must match on amount before reconciling; correspondence is re-checked when a bill is edited after initial booking.

INV-11 confirmed: no separate GL account per counterparty - a payables GL account with a counterparty property, keeping a single account balance sliceable by counterparty.

VAT recognition: when an invoice's expense is split across periods (e.g. Mar-Apr-May), the full VAT amount books to the balance sheet (VAT reclaimable/payable) on the invoice date - VAT is not split monthly with the expense.

FX rate is booked at the ECB daily reference (mid) rate on the transaction date, frozen on the line; when the settling payment clears at a different rate the residual is a realised FX gain/loss posted to a dedicated FX-difference account, and a separate bank FX fee books to bank charges.

VAT corrections are always corrected forward; two VAT balance-sheet accounts (normal + corrections/control); once the EUR 1,000 cumulative threshold is crossed all subsequent corrections route to the corrections account until the suppletie is filed. <EUR 1,000 net/year rolls into the next return, >EUR 1,000 goes on a supplementary return.

VAT is a first-class dimension: VAT code on base and tax lines; treatment (domestic / reverse-charge / intra-EU / import / export) drives the posting shape; the return maps codes to boxes.

VAT corrections after a period close are booked in the next period (dated day 1); under EUR 1,000 fold into the next return without a supplemental filing. Balance sheet needs three VAT lines: receivable, payable, corrections/suspense.
Closed periods lock writes by default; unlocking is approval-gated and only for material post-close accruals; insert-only with full audit log.
Insert-only ledger with reversals - no edits to journal entries; corrections reverse and rebook. Period closes define immutability. Monitoring over rollback. Euro-only, multi-currency deferred.

Neno Ledger went live on production for Ocean Ionics (NEO-1361 + NEO-1514): it books bank transactions on arrival, bills on confirmation, and transaction links (settlement); pre-existing bills/transactions raise expected Ledger Failures handled via a bank-transaction backfill script (Runbook 'Settlement upstream leg is not live'); the neno-vs-Exact trial-balance comparison page is not yet useful on OI due to data noise.

Bill edit/re-book after booking: because the ledger locks a booked bill's facts, an Edit button books a reversing entry for the bill and any related settlement to release the evidence, and a Re-book button commits a fresh booking; multiple edits are allowed before re-booking and the existing Exact sync flow is unaffected.

meetings.summary: Matthew, Ihor, Venla, Andries and Eugenia worked through the depreciation option space and settled most of v1. Mixed bills allow individual line items to be capitalised with the rest going to an expense GL. The accountant picks an asset group and a start date and the system derives the end date from the group's policy - equipment five years, machinery ten - so no useful-life field is needed. The capitalisation threshold is a neno house rule of EUR 400 per item, with no per-customer flexibility for now. Items are grouped by invoice line, and adding an eleventh laptop later is a new asset entry. Assets not yet in service park in an asset suspense account and are reclassified on activation; VAT-exempt clients capitalise the full inc-VAT value with the VAT code set to zero; fully depreciated assets stay in the register at zero book value. Disposal only needs to distinguish proceeds from no proceeds, and monthly posting is right for every current client. Two gaps in the current v1 became explicit requirements: schedules must be editable, and fixed-asset accounts need a path for legitimate non-capitalisation uses such as opening balances and reclassifications. Disposal date and partial disposal were left unresolved.
decisions: Mixed bills: select individual line items to capitalise, the rest to expense GL
Asset group plus start date; the end date derives from group policy, no manual useful-life entry
EUR 400 per item capitalisation threshold as a neno house rule
Assets not yet in service park in an asset suspense account until activation
VAT-exempt clients capitalise the full inc-VAT value with the VAT code set to zero
Monthly depreciation cadence; disposal distinguishes only proceeds from no proceeds
